evidenceFindings.finding: Endorses open movement in principle but opposes unlimited immigration while a welfare state persists.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Conditional immigration inference keeps the actual welfare constraint rather than manufacturing detailed visa requirements.

evidenceFindings.finding: Opposed Iraq invasion as aggression but wanted success after entry; campaigned for voluntary rather than conscript forces.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Qualified anti-aggression assessment is not absolute pacifism or rejection of all defensive threats.

evidenceFindings.finding: Advocates private enterprise and private school operation even with publicly financed vouchers.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Qualified competitive-provider inference separates financing from ownership and leaves genuine monopoly cases unresolved.

evidenceFindings.finding: Explicitly defends unilateral free trade and rejects retaliatory/protective tariffs because they harm consumers.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Direct doctrine applied to the specified barrier; strategic control and procurement exceptions are not silently ignored.

evidenceFindings.finding: Market pricing, opposition to wage controls/minimum wage, voluntary transactions and a monetary rule define his economic programme.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Direct economic-doctrine inference; support for monetary discipline is not evidence of any precise private-currency arrangement.

evidenceFindings.finding: Negative income tax supports a poverty floor and low-paid earnings; supports a single-rate income tax rather than equalized outcomes.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Distribution assessment separates effective average burdens under allowances from uniform marginal rates, and eligibility from arbitrary expiry.

evidenceFindings.finding: Noncoercion in private beliefs follows from his stated limited-government position.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Qualified civil-authority inference; vouchers for religious schools do not imply a religious foundation of state law.

evidenceFindings.finding: School essay describes technology-driven structural changes and competitive innovation.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Qualified productivity/displacement analogy does not establish brain-implant, embryo or ecosystem safety thresholds.

evidenceFindings.finding: Public-school argument emphasizes decentralization and voluntary choice over centralized provision.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Limited fiscal/educational decentralization inference does not establish secession or every police/health jurisdiction.

evidenceFindings.finding: In the 1991 interview Friedman expressly endorses Mill’s mature-adult self-regarding liberty principle and compares personal drug risk to voluntary skydiving and skiing.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Qualified healthy-adult implant analogy: adequate basic safety and informed competent consent do not justify prohibition solely for the user’s long-term personal risk. Concrete harm to others or compromised future agency/consent would alter the premise; no clinical safety forecast is attributed to Friedman.
